meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law in Hong Kong SAR under PRC constitutional framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: For the HKSAR: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) (AMLO) and its Schedules 2 and 5; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 17A (Significant Controllers Register); Limited Partnership Funds Ordinance (Cap. 637) sections 5 and 49; Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) section 88; UN Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537); UN (Anti-Terrorism Measures) Ordinance (Cap. 575). For the PRC: PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective 1 November 2024) on Beneficial Owner Information Administration; PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (as amended); PRC Partnership Enterprise Law (as amended); SAMR Measures for Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises (2010); SAMR and PBOC Beneficial Owner Filing Rules for Market Entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Registration Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (or SAR registry issuing the foreign-invested partnership or private foundation vehicle certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize original official certificate by a qualified notary in the issuing jurisdiction; if issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention state (HKSAR or Mainland China), obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority (HKSAR High Court Registry Authentication Unit for HKSAR; PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or delegated provincial foreign affairs office for Mainland China); do not add consular legalization on the Apostille path. If the issuing state is not an Apostille member, notarize, then legalize through the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then apply for diplomatic/consular legalization at the consulate or embassy of the destination jurisdiction, then translate into English.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Continuing Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (or applicable Registrar of Partnerships)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: obtain certificate, notarize if required, and apostille through HKSAR High Court Registry or PRC MOFA for Mainland-origin documents. Consular path only if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention member: notarize, then origin MOFA legalization, then destination consulate/embassy legalization, then English translation. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Partners Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing filing agents and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / Managing Partners / Founder's Council of the private charitable foundation entity, authenticated by a Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Origin notarization by notary in the state where the resolution is executed; if the execution state is Apostille-capable, apostille through the competent authority; if not, execute consular legalization of the notarized document with the destination Hong Kong/China consulate. Provide English sworn translation after authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement / Foundation Deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders, partners and legal counsel; certified copy notarized by a Hong Kong notary public or PRC notary office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Mainland/HK origin: notarize by notary office, apostille through PRC MOFA/PFAA or HKSAR High Court Registry, then submit to Hong Kong Companies Registry/IRD/bank. Consular path for non-Apostille jurisdictions: notarize, origin MOFA legalization, destination consular legalization, then English translation. Apostille and consular legalization remain mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank (e.g., an authorized institution in Hong Kong or a major international bank in the jurisdiction of the proposed source of funds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank to issue letter on secure bank letterhead; banks commonly provide a direct banker's confirmation to the receiving Hong Kong corporate bank; if an authentication certificate is required, apostille by the bank's jurisdiction competent authority when Apostille Convention applies, otherwise use consular legalization. The bank reference letter should not be legalized twice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration / Significant Controllers Register Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or designated corporate services provider maintaining the Significant Controllers Register under Cap. 622 Part 17A; for Mainland FIP, the SAMR/PBOC beneficial ownership filing acknowledgement.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified extract notarized by the notary of the place of the register; if the register is in HKSAR or Mainland China, use Apostille path through High Court Registry or PRC MOFA. If the register is kept in a non-Apostille jurisdiction, use consular legalization of the notarized extract. No sequential chaining of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every beneficial owner, partner, director, trustee, officer, signatory, informed person and intended grant counterparty against the FATF Recommendations, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN plus non-SDN lists, HKSAR sanctioned and designated persons under AMLO Cap. 615 and the UN Sanctions Ordinance, and PRC domestic counter-terrorism and money laundering lists. PEP identification must use real-time electronic PEP databases (Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check or equivalent), adverse media screening, sanctions ownership-rule analysis and control-link tracing. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, family offices, high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed non-profit end-users and non-face-to-face grant recipients. All findings must be documented in a risk-based CDD/EDD file, with senior management approval for any residual-risk acceptance, ongoing transaction monitoring for grants and wire transfers, and suspicious transaction report filing to the Hong Kong Joint Financial Intelligence Unit under AMLO section 25A.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry / Company Name Search Portal (https://www.eregistry.gov.hk; integrated with ICRIS) and, for a Mainland-invested partnership component, the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System under SAMR
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Hong Kong company names may be English and/or Chinese; Chinese names must use Traditional Chinese characters and must be transliterated consistently with the existing Companies Registry name index; English names use English alphabets. Where a foreign-element or charitable foundation name is used, the name should comprise a distinctive element plus a descriptive business-scope element plus the legal-form suffix, and phonetic equivalents of an existing registered name will be treated as identical or misleadingly similar. The four-tier naming convention requires review of (i) the distinctive mark, (ii) the proposed charitable endowment activity, (iii) the legal form designation (Foundation, Limited Partnership, LPF, Company), and (iv) the statutory suffix required for liability disclosure, all in a single integrated clearance pass.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice from the Hong Kong Companies Registry, the applicant should immediately obtain the written grounds and request an expedited reconsideration by filing a formal submission to the Registrar of Companies with corrected name candidates and supporting evidence of ministerial or regulator consent where a sensitive token was involved. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file an appeal to the Administrative Appeals Board or seek judicial review before the Court of First Instance under HKSAR administrative law, within the statutory time limit. In parallel, the applicant should reserve fall-back names through the e-Registry portal because the 20-day name reservation window is not extendable and any lapse requires a fresh application with a new reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the bare registered-office statutory requirement under the Companies Ordinance or Partnership Ordinance, but it is materially inconsistent with the commercial substance expected by the Inland Revenue Department for a charitable foundation or endowment-management entity and is generally rejected by Hong Kong banks under HKMA anti-money-laundering guidance when the intended rail is bank wire and grant distribution. The IRD will likely deny Section 88 charitable exemption, the HK Companies Registry may query the registered address, and the HKMA bank onboarding process will require a physical principal place of business where directors/partners receive visitors, records are kept, and controllers can be interviewed for UBO and source-of-funds verification. A virtual office is acceptable only as an ancillary correspondence point if a separate physical registered office and a local managing partner or company secretary are maintained with exclusive custody of books and records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspection risk is quantitatively estimated at 45% in the first 24 months if the foundation operates from a virtual office without local staff. The inspection checklist includes: no physical business sign, no named local manager, no original statutory books, no segregated partnership/foundation records, no local payroll or employment records, inconsistent grant distribution trail, mass mail-forwarding address, and bank account with no HK director/partner involvement. The IRD, Companies Registry, and HKMA-regulated banks may conduct physical site visits, and the police and the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit may inspect under Cap. 615 if suspicion arises. Maintaining a bona fide Hong Kong administrative office, local third-party service provider, local meeting minutes, independent audit trail, and clearly identified grant beneficiaries reduces the inspection probability to below 10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), ss. 4-8; Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 337), ss. 4-10; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), ss. 2, 6 and 8; Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), s. 88; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), Sch. 1; Trustee Ordinance (Cap. 29) insofar as it applies to the stewardship of donated endowment assets. Because the entity is a Foreign-Invested Partnership, the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) is not the primary formation statute, but its name-restriction, director analogue, and corporate governance principles are applied by best practice and by the Foundation Deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section, 14th Floor, High Block, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong, together with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Statement of Registration of a Limited Partnership) and Form IRBR/BR (Application for Business Registration), filed through the one-stop Companies Registry e-Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a Foreign-Invested Partnership. The Foundation Deed may set a nominal capital account of one Hong Kong dollar or any agreed endowment amount, and no blocked escrow account is required. Contributions are governed exclusively by the executed Foundation Deed and Limited Partnership Agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Board of Directors Resolution of the Foreign-Invested Partnership (Private Charitable Foundation). WHEREAS, this Foreign-Invested Partnership, being the legal vehicle for a Private Charitable Foundation classified under ISIC 6430 and NAICS 813211, is to be formed and registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the exclusive charitable purpose of endowment management for philanthropic and scientific grants; and WHEREAS, the Partnership does not issue share capital but will maintain capital account subscriptions by the general partners that are functionally equivalent to share subscriptions under the governing Foundation Deed; and WHEREAS, the Directors, General Partners and Governors have reviewed the proposed Foundation Deed, the Limited Partnership Agreement, the name-search certificate, the registered office arrangements, the proposed banking mandates and the intended application to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue under Section 88 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. Formation Approval. The formation and registration of the Foreign-Invested Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, Cap. 337, is hereby authorised and approved, and the Managing Partner is directed to file Form LP1 and the related business registration application without delay. 2. Capital Account Subscription. Each general partner shall execute the Foundation Deed and subscribe to the capital account set forth in the schedule to that Deed, and the absence of a separate share capital shall not limit the fiduciary duties of the partners with respect to endowment preservation and charitable distribution. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Partnership in Hong Kong shall be adopted as stated in the Foundation Deed, and the Founding Partner is directed to evidence the same by tenancy agreement, occupancy letter and written acceptance of the registered office. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following officers are hereby appointed, with full power to act severally or jointly as provided in the Deed: the Managing Partner, the Foundation Secretary, the Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer, and the Authorised Representatives to the Companies Registry and the Inland Revenue Department. Each appointee shall hold office until removed by ordinary resolution of the partners and shall discharge all statutory duties under Cap. 38, Cap. 337, Cap. 310 and Cap. 615. 5. Banking Authorisation. The Partnership shall open charitable endowment bank accounts at one or more licensed banks in Hong Kong, and any two board-designated signatories shall be jointly authorised to execute cheques, wire transfers and grant distribution instructions. The banking mandate is to be authenticated by the notarised resolution and deposited with the presenting bank. 6. Tax and Charitable Recognition. The officers are directed to apply to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue for recognition as a charitable institution within the meaning of Section 88 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance and to provide all financial statements, grant-making policies and constitutional documents required in support thereof. 7. General Authority. All acts done by the officers, agents and professional advisers prior to the adoption of this Resolution in connection with the formation, banking, licensing and registration of the Partnership are hereby ratified, confirmed and adopted as acts of the Partnership. This Resolution is binding on all present and future partners, governors, directors, officers, successors and assigns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Clearance and Constitutional Document Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section, through the e-Registry portal and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a live name-search in the Companies Registry to confirm that the proposed Foreign-Invested Partnership name and any Chinese name are not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, limited partnership, trademark or restricted expression such as Foundation, Trust, Limited or Bank. Prepare and execute the Foundation Deed and the Limited Partnership Agreement in English with an optional certified Chinese translation. Ensure each foreign general partner obtains an apostilled or legalised certificate of good standing and consular authentication as required by the home jurisdiction. Submit the preliminary name clearance application with a cover letter identifying the proposed charitable objects and confirming the absence of unlawful purposes. Obtain written name clearance before proceeding to the formal filing, and retain an independent Hong Kong solicitor to authenticate the execution page of the Foundation Deed.
required_dossiers: Original notarised passport or national identity document of each general partner
Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent from the foreign partner's home registry
Residential address proof for each individual partner dated within the last three months
Original signed Foundation Deed and Limited Partnership Agreement
Local Authorised Representative or Agent consent form
Proposed name search and preliminary name clearance application
Apostilled corporate resolutions of any corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry flags the proposed name as confusingly similar or as containing a restricted term, file a written submission establishing distinguishability and, where relevant, written consent from the existing name holder. If the objection is maintained, resubmit the entire name-clearance package under a revised distinguishing name within three working days. If the Registry suspends the application for suspected non-compliance, cure the defect by supplying the original notarial certifications and a legal opinion on the charitable objects, then request expedited review by the Limited Partnerships Section.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration of the Foreign-Invested Partnership and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section, and Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, via one-stop e-Registry filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP1 and the Business Registration application in the exact statutory format, with the full registered office address in Hong Kong and the full names of all general and limited partners. Submit the executed original package to the Companies Registry together with the Foundation Deed, a certified copy of the tenancy or licence of the registered office, and a declaration of compliance executed by every general partner. Pay the prescribed Companies Registry and Business Registration fees and submit the Foundation Deed for stamp duty assessment. After the Companies Registry issues the Certificate of Registration of the Limited Partnership, the Business Registration Office will issue the Business Registration Certificate. Immediately verify the legal entity number, date of registration, partner particulars and service of process address, and notify the Managing Partner of the registered date so that bank opening and tax applications can commence without delay.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 in duplicate
Application for Business Registration (Form IRBR/BR)
Certified true copy of the executed Foundation Deed and Limited Partnership Agreement
Evidence of registered office address in Hong Kong such as tenancy agreement or occupancy licence
Declaration of compliance signed by all general partners
Filing fee payment vouchers and stamp duty assessment form
Original name clearance letter from the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a requisition on Form LP1, respond in writing within the stated period, normally fourteen calendar days, with a marked-up deed and a solicitor's confirmation of the corrections. If the Business Registration Office questions the fee or applicable waiver, submit the Foundation Deed and an explanation of charitable purpose and request a determination under Section 8 of the Business Registration Ordinance. If the Registrar refuses registration, seek administrative reconsideration by letter and thereafter file an appeal to the Court of First Instance where legally available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Section 88 Charitable Exemption and Tax Recognition Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commissioner of Inland Revenue, Charitable Institutions and Trusts Section, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a formal application letter addressed to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue requesting the recognition of the Foreign-Invested Partnership as a charitable foundation under Section 88 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance. The application must demonstrate that the objects of the Foundation are exclusively charitable in law, that no profit may be distributed to partners, and that the endowment management activity is confined to philanthropic and scientific grant-making and lawful investment of donated capital. Include the executed Foundation Deed, Business Registration Certificate, three-year projected financial statements, the grant-making policy, the conflicts-of-interest policy, and the list of governors and statutory officers. Submit one certified copy to the Charitable Institutions and Trusts Section and retain stamped receipts. If the IRD requires amendments to the objects clause, execute a supplementary deed and resubmit the amended deed with a table marking each change. Continue to operate only in a manner consistent with the charitable purposes during the recognition period.
required_dossiers: Application letter under Section 88, Inland Revenue Ordinance
Certified copy of the registered Foundation Deed and Limited Partnership Agreement
Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Three-year projected financial statements and grant distribution plan
Philanthrophic and scientific grant-making policy including conflicts-of-interest rules
Identity and background documents for all governors, partners and statutory officers
Legal opinion from a Hong Kong solicitor confirming exclusively charitable objects
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department issues an inquiry or refuses recognition, respond with a solicitors legal opinion, amend the objects clause by supplementary deed, and resubmit the complete package. Request a conference with the Charitable Institutions and Trusts Section to clarify any doubts on endowment management activities. If final refusal is issued, pursue administrative review by letter to the Commissioner and, if necessary, judicial review to the Court of First Instance in accordance with applicable constitutional and administrative law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Anti-Money Laundering and Statutory Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Trust and Company Service Provider Licensing Section, and the Partnership's internal Compliance Officer under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, Cap. 615.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a written Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism manual containing customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, record retention and suspicious transaction reporting procedures. Appoint a Compliance Officer and a Money Laundering Reporting Officer by separate board resolution and file the designations in the internal register. If the Foreign-Invested Partnership will only manage its own endowment capital, prepare and retain a written exemption analysis on the application of the Trust or Company Service Provider licensing regime under Schedule 1 of Cap. 615. If the Partnership intends to administer third-party trusts or act as a trustee for charitable collections, apply for a Trust or Company Service Provider licence before carrying on that regulated activity. Register the beneficial owners of the Partnership in the significant controllers register and ensure all donors and grantees are screened against sanctions and politically exposed person databases.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT manual and risk assessment signed by the Compliance Officer
Appointment letter for the Compliance Officer
Appointment letter for the Money Laundering Reporting Officer
Beneficial ownership register and significant controllers register
Sanctions screening policy and politically exposed person policy
TCSP licence exemption analysis or TCSP licence application, as applicable
Customer due diligence templates for grant recipients
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry queries the TCSP licensing position, file a legal opinion and a sworn declaration from the Managing Partner that the Partnership acts solely for its own charitable endowment and not for third parties. If a licence is nevertheless required, submit the TCSP application immediately. If penalties are proposed under Cap. 615, make written representations before assessment, preserve all documentary evidence of the exemption analysis, and, if necessary, request a personal hearing with the licensing authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking Activation, Registered Office Occupation and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed banks, Fire Services Department, and Buildings Department under the Hong Kong public safety framework.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the banking resolution and open the charitable endowment bank account with a licensed bank in Hong Kong, presenting the certificate of registration, the deducted-s88 recognition status, the Foundation Deed, specimen signatures and the AML manual. Obtain a signed bank mandate requiring joint authorisation for disbursement and separate approval for grant distribution instructions. For the registered office and any executive office, arrange a Fire Services Department compliance inspection covering means of escape, emergency lighting, fire extinguishers and any installed alarm system. Arrange a Buildings Department structural load review if the premises are in an old commercial building, and obtain confirmation that the intended office use is permitted under the lease and the Building (Planning) Regulations. Keep copies of all approvals in the statutory records and file the fire safety compliance certificate with the Foundation Secretary.
required_dossiers: Bank account application forms and joint signatory mandate
Original or certified copy of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate and Section 88 recognition/acknowledgement letter if issued
Original board resolution authorising bank account opening
AML manual and beneficial owner register
Fire safety compliance certificate or inspection report
Buildings Department means-of-escape and structural load approval where applicable
Lease, occupancy certificate and registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application or requests enhanced due diligence, obtain a written refusal explanation and provide independent legal opinions, source-of-funds declarations and a letter of comfort from the Inland Revenue Department confirming that the Section 88 application is active. If the Fire Services Department issues a fire safety improvement notice, complete the remedial works within the stated compliance period and provide certified photographs and an engineer's report. If the Buildings Department rejects the occupation certificate, cure the non-conformity through licensed structural engineers and re-submit the drawings with a revised application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Charitable Institutions and Trusts Section, together with the Companies Registry, Business Registration Office. No industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing permit is applicable to ISIC 6430 endowment management; the competent authority is the Hong Kong tax registry and, for premises safety, the Fire Services Department and Buildings Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate and Section 88 Charitable Exemption Reference; no separate manufacturing operating permit, industrial license or EIA authorization is required because the activity is administrative, financial and philanthropic rather than physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Exempt. The Foreign-Invested Partnership will conduct only office-based endowment management and grant distribution, and therefore does not fall within any project or category requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance, Cap. 499. The correct classification is Environmental Registration Exemption for a purely administrative office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to industrial wastewater, VOCs or hazardous waste because no industrial process is carried out. Domestic sanitary sewage from staff restrooms must be discharged to the municipal sewer under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance, Cap. 358, in accordance with the Drainage Services Department standards. If a standby generator or cooling tower is installed, any emissions must comply with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance, Cap. 311, and any chlorinated cooling tower bleed discharge must meet the relevant EPD licence limits. No hazardous waste stream is expected; any used electrical equipment must be handled under the Waste Disposal Ordinance, Cap. 354.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Services Department fire safety inspection and, where applicable, certificate under the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance, Cap. 502, covering means of escape, emergency lighting, fire alarm and extinguishing appliances. Buildings Department review of structural load and means of escape for the registered office. Occupational safety and health approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance, Cap. 509, including workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, waste segregation and first-aid provisions. No Civil Defense industrial fire permit is applicable because there are no scheduled dangerous goods, chemical processes or high-risk manufacturing activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, administered through the national Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal and the relevant provincial STA e-Tax systems; tax registration data is integrated through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). For the Hong Kong SAR non-resident interest, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of Hong Kong SAR is the competent authority for issuing resident person certificates under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement through the eTAX portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the PRC multi-license integration regime, the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) is first registered with the local SAMR office; the issued business license contains the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for mainland China. No separate tax registration application is normally required because SAMR automatically transmits registration data to the STA. The FIP must then activate its account on the provincial Electronic Tax Bureau, complete real-name authentication, update taxpayer classification (small-scale or VAT general taxpayer), apply for invoice quotas and digital invoice systems, and complete any required charitable foundation or fund registration with the competent ministry if the entity will act as a private charitable foundation. Foreign non-resident partners do not receive a separate PRC TIN for the partnership, but their identity, residency, and profit-allocation percentages must be reported to the STA in the partnership registration and annual information returns; a Hong Kong partner that seeks treaty benefits must obtain an IRD Certificate of Resident Person and file it with the STA before reduced withholding rates are applied.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity classification election. A Foreign-Invested Partnership is compulsorily transparent for enterprise income tax purposes under Cai Shui [2008] No.159; the partnership itself is not taxed on its profits, and each partner is subject to enterprise income tax or individual income tax on its allocable share. VAT registration, by contrast, is imposed at the entity level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, governed by the PRC VAT Law and implementation regulations and administered by the State Taxation Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to obtaining the initial tax registration because the USCC is issued at market registration. Compulsory registration as a VAT general taxpayer arises when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 (excluding VAT); below RMB 5,000,000, a FIP may remain a small-scale taxpayer and apply the simplified levy rate, or it may voluntarily register as a general taxpayer if it has fixed places of business and satisfactory accounting. Charitable grants alone are normally outside the VAT taxable scope because they are not consideration for a supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA operates the National VAT Invoice Integrated Service Platform as the sole lawful invoice-issuing and verification environment. VAT invoices must be issued through the platform using an STA-approved tax UKey or the fully digitalized electronic invoice system; the tax authority assigns the invoice code and frame number, applies an encrypted digital signature or electronic seal, and records the invoice in the Nationwide VAT Invoice Verification Platform. Input VAT credit on special VAT invoices is accepted only after the invoice is electronically matched and reconciled on the platform. Real-time or batch clearance is mandatory for all general taxpayers, and pilot businesses are required to adopt the all-electronic invoice without physical paper forms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods physically shipped from mainland China and customs-cleared may be zero-rated (0%

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with rigorous foreign exchange controls administered by SAFE. The Renminbi is freely convertible on the current account for legitimate trade, service, and non-trade payments, including grants and charitable transfers, provided the underlying authenticity and documentation satisfy SAFE's business authenticity and compliance review. However, the capital account remains tightly regulated; a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) receiving capital injections from Hong Kong must register the inbound remittance through the SAFE foreign direct investment (FDI) information system, and the foreign currency funds must be held in a designated capital account pending verification. Once registered, the FIP may convert the capital to RMB for permitted operational expenditures under the national negative list regime, but any alteration in the use of funds or onward capital transfer to a third party requires a supplementary filing. From a treasury perspective, distributions to foreign partners or cross-border grant payments are treated as current account outflows that require only evidence of tax clearance and action by the managing partner, not prior SAFE approval. Large or frequent recurring philanthropic flows from an overseas related foundation may, however, be re-characterised as capital account transactions by the bank's compliance department, necessitating additional approvals. Overall, profit or donation remittances are suspended only when sanctioned partners or unverified recipient jurisdictions are involved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Rules on Foreign Exchange Administration of Export Proceeds (SAFE Circular 2012/1), a Chinese enterprise, including a FIP with an export licence, must repatriate all export proceeds into a domestic foreign exchange current-account account within 180 days of the export customs declaration; the deadline may be extended to 12 months if the enterprise is rated A-class by the customs/SAFE joint accreditation. There is no mandatory fixed percentage conversion to RMB; instead, the enterprise may retain the foreign currency up to an SAFE-approved settlement account quota, selling all amounts above the quota to a designated bank at the market mid-price. For a charitable endowment entity without export operations, the rule has no application, but the FIP must nevertheless observe any other repatriation obligations triggered by foreign interest or donation income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Exchange Capital Account) and Basic Operational RMB Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Exchange Capital Account) and Basic Operational RMB Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and General Operational RMB Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs), whether domestic or offshore, cannot serve as the primary banking infrastructure for a mainland-incorporated FIP. Under the Banking Supervision Law and the Regulations on the Administration of E-money Payments, only licensed commercial banks may maintain clearing accounts and provide foreign exchange conversion services; EMIs are limited to supporting prepaid instruments and payment aggregations without deposit-taking functions. Therefore, any Hong Kong or offshore digital EMI proposal, including those offering virtual accounts or multi-currency wallets, is legally barred from replacing a Tier-1 PRC bank. An EMI may be considered only as an ancillary channel for highly controlled pass-through payments, but the FIP's treasury policy should require that all settlement rails terminate at a licensed Chinese bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory managing partner must appear in person at a Chinese bank branch for the initial onboarding, at which time the original partnership registration certificate, the foreign-invested partnership licence, and the identities of all partners will be verified. Non-resident partners may, at the bank's discretion, complete a face-to-face interview before a Chinese consular officer in their country of residence or at an overseas branch of the same bank (e.g., BOC Hong Kong). The FIP itself must have a registered business address in mainland China and a statutory representative available for a local interview. Remote video-based verification is generally not permitted for the first account opening, although for subsequent additional signatories it is acceptable under the bank's internal video-KYC protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient explanation of the source of the initial endowment capital, particularly when routed through a Hong Kong holding company with no clear economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report prepared by a Hong Kong certified public accountant, audited financial statements of the holding company, the notarised gift or trust deed, the donor's latest personal asset declaration, and a legal opinion from a PRC attorney confirming that the funds are clean and the FIP has received the required charitable registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the registered charitable objective and the proposed beneficiary countries, which may include sanctions-affected or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the complete grant policy manual, the list of proposed beneficiaries with registration evidence, sanctions/PEPS screening outputs from a recognised commercial database, the grant agreements, and the consideration of the relevant UN resolutions and China's export-control list. Include minutes of the foundation's grant committee demonstrating that a thorough risk assessment was performed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of a politically exposed person (PEP) or an individual with adverse media on the partner roster, creating enhanced due diligence triggers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an independent PEP/adverse-media report from a licensed external due-diligence vendor (Dow Jones, Refinitiv, or equivalent), an affidavit from the PEP explaining the legitimate source of funds and purpose, proof of the PEP's official position and accountability, and a notarised authorisation allowing the bank to make a direct inquiry with the relevant supervisory authority if needed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent use of the capital escrow account, with a likelihood of capital formation for hidden investment or round-tripping activities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a treasury policy and annual spending plan approved by the board, an irrevocable undertaking that the capital account will only be debited for approved philanthropic distributions, the FIP's AML/CFT internal controls (if applicable), and an agreement to provide quarterly informational reports to the bank on fund flows and counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funding from Hong Kong or other offshore sources should be routed via SWIFT MT103 into the FIP's foreign exchange capital account at a designated Chinese bank. The remittance instruction must carry the SAFE-specified code for a foreign direct investment capital contribution (identified as FDI Capital Injection in the bank's BOP reporting system) and include the FIP's name, the SAFE registration number, and a clear payment reference to the partnership agreement. Upon receipt, the bank will conduct a compliance review and hold the funds for mandatory capital verification by an independent PRC certified public accountant, after which the funds are available for conversion to RMB and permitted expenditure. Any change to the investment amount must be pre-registered with SAFE via the relevant filing platform.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Grant disbursements and trade-related payments should be executed through the FIP's settlement bank using SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for donations, scholarships, or scientific grants; the payment must reference the underlying grant agreement and use the applicable SAFE outbound purpose code for philanthropic contributions. If the FIP's endowment engages in trade finance arrangements (such as purchasing equipment or funding proof-of-concept trials), it may also utilise Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) or Documentary Collections (MT400) through the same bank. All outbound payments require the managing partner's authorisation, a completed tax withholding certificate where relevant, and an anti-money-laundering check of the recipient against the sanction list.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts with tenors up to 12 months executed through the domestic bank's derivatives desk (non-deliverable forwards are not permitted for onshore FIPs)
Cross-currency swaps (RMB/USD) for large endowment capital if a natural hedge is created by long-term grant liabilities
Zero-cost collars or participating forwards for the FIP's projected foreign-currency grant disbursement needs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal (Business Registration Ordinance, Cap 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before expiry date of the current one-year certificate; renewal notice is issued approximately one month before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts an additional HK$300 (USD 38.46) per certificate; continued non-payment is an offence punishable by a fine of up to HK$5,000 (USD 641.03) and the Business Registration may be cancelled or deregistered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return - Form BIR52 for Partnerships (Inland Revenue Ordinance, Cap 112)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the return; for a 31 March year of assessment, returns are typically issued on 1 April and due by 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse: fine up to HK$10,000 (USD 1,282.05) and possible tax penalty equal to three times the undercharged tax; the IRD may raise an estimated assessment and prosecute persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions - Form BIR56A and Individual Forms BIR56B (if employees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Employer Returns Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after issuance; for most employers the annual payroll return is required by 1 July following the end of the year of assessment on 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur penalties up to HK$1,500 (USD 192.31) per form for employers; repeated default can lead to prosecution and additional fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return - Form NAR1 (applicable only if the charitable foundation is incorporated as a company; not required for a pure Foreign-Invested Partnership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If delivered after 42 days: HK$1,200 (USD 153.85) additional fee up to 3 months; HK$2,400 (USD 307.69) for 3-6 months; HK$3,600 (USD 461.54) for over 6 months; persistent default may lead to prosecution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Charity Return / Audited Financial Statements submitted to maintain Section 88 Inland Revenue Ordinance tax-exempt status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Commissioner of Inland Revenue (Charities Section)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the foundation's financial year-end, or as stated on the IRD notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or failure to provide audited accounts may lead to withdrawal of tax exemption, revised assessment, revocation of charitable registration, and disqualification of the foundation from receiving tax-deductible donations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For Hong Kong companies under Companies Ordinance (Cap 622), an independent certified audit is mandatory unless the company qualifies as a small private company or a member of a small private company group meeting at least two of three tests for the financial year: total annual revenue not exceeding HKD 25 million, total assets not exceeding HKD 25 million, and no more than 50 employees; the audit may be waived only by a unanimous members' resolution. For a Foreign-Invested Partnership, the partnership legislation does not impose a turnover/asset audit threshold, but a certified independent audit is statutorily required by the Inland Revenue Department for any charitable institution claiming Section 88 exemption where the foundation has annual gross income exceeding HKD 5 million or total assets exceeding HKD 10 million; charitable grant-making foundations with any public fundraising must in practice have audited financial statements in all accounting periods.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS); eligible private entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) or the SME Financial Reporting Framework; charitable foundations should also follow the Inland Revenue Department's accounting and financial reporting guidelines for charitable institutions and the HKICPA's applicable standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require an annual UBO confirmation certificate for partnerships. Companies must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) and update it within 7 days of any change. The Annual Return NAR1, due within 42 days of the incorporation anniversary, confirms the register of members and directors. For share allotments or transfers of partnership interests, the relevant register must be amended promptly and any allotment of shares must be reported to the Companies Registry within 30 days on Form NSC1; for an FIP, transfers of partnership interests must be recorded in the Register of Partners within 30 days to preserve pass-through status and limited liability protection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Members'/Partners' and Directors' Resolutions
Register of Partners and Capital Contributions
Significant Controllers Register (if the foundation is incorporated as a company)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,500 per annum for registered office, corporate secretarial and compliance agent services in Hong Kong
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 20,000 per annum for a certified audit of a small charitable endowment partnership; USD 20,000 - USD 60,000 for complex grant and investment portfolios

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% standard rate; 8.25% concessionary rate for first HK$2 million assessable profits under two-tiered profits tax regime
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Charitable foundation profits exemption under Section 88 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO); 100% R&D super deduction; territorial source taxation (offshore passive income not taxable)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return – Partnership (BIR52) filed electronically via the Hong Kong e-Tax portal (GovHK)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline is 1 month from the date of issue of the return; electronic filing through a tax representative extends the deadline to 15 November for fiscal year ending 31 March (grace up to 3 months)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and Business Registration Number of the partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as registered under the Business Registration Ordinance and the 8-digit certificate number. For a non-resident partnership, disclose the local tax representative's details if no office is maintained in Hong Kong.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address in Hong Kong
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity must provide a residential address of a partner or the business address of the tax representative. Failure to provide a local address may lead to the return being deemed non-filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period covered by the return (from / to)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the 12-month period audited. If the period is shorter than 12 months due to commencement or cessation, attach the balance sheet and profit & loss account. Non-resident partnerships must align the period with the foreign fiscal year if different, and obtain an IRD change of year-end approval.

Describe the principal activities in detail, for example 'endowment management for philanthropic grants'. This is critical for determining the territorial source of profits. Non-residents should distinguish between Hong Kong-sourced and offshore-sourced income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable profits before deductions (or loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Hong Kong-sourced profits. If all income is derived offshore, apply the offshore claim (see field note) and declare zero assessable profits. The IRD may challenge the claim; maintain full source evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's share of assessable profits / loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List the name, taxpayer ID, and profit-sharing ratio of each partner (including non-resident partners). The assessable profit is allocated per the partnership deed. Non-resident partners are taxable on the Hong Kong source share; no withholding is required at the partnership level, but they must file personal/profits tax in Hong Kong.

Include approved charitable donations, depreciation, and other deductible expenses. For a charitable foundation, expenditure on scientific grants may be deductible if made to an approved charitable institution. Non-resident partnerships must keep receipts and ensure the payments have been actually made out of assessable profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable profits after adjustments and allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry forward the adjusted amount from Box 7. Deductions are not automatic; the IRD will verify the eligibility. For non-residents, do not deduct expenses that are not in the production of Hong Kong-sourced profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable calculated on net assessable profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the two-tiered rate: 8.25% on the first HK$2 million of assessable profits per partnership (not per partner?) and 16.5% above that. If the partnership is a charitable institution itself, tax may be nil. Non-resident partners may claim foreign tax credit relief under a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signature by tax representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax representative must sign the declaration, confirming that all information is correct. A non-resident partnership must appoint a tax representative in Hong Kong before the return is issued, otherwise a late filing penalty will apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty HK$1,200; additional penalties up to HK$10,000 if return is over 6 months late, plus 10% of tax undercharged. Wilful tax evasion under section 82 of the IRO: fine up to HK$50,000, three times the amount of undercharged tax, imprisonment up to 3 years. Civil penalties for incorrect returns under section 82A may be up to 100% of the tax undercharged.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Hong Kong imposes 0% withholding tax on dividends paid by a Hong Kong entity to both residents and non-residents. If the partnership is treated as a Chinese enterprise for PRC tax purposes (e.g., central management and control in China), dividends distributed to non-China shareholders may be subject to China's 10% dividend withholding tax under the Enterprise Income Tax Law, subject to treaty relief.

stage_6.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced China–HK DTA rate (5% for dividends on a 25% holding; 7% for interest and royalties), the recipient must be the beneficial owner and a Hong Kong tax resident. The protocol requires: (1) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Inland Revenue Department (IRF 131); (2) complete a Certificate of Resident Status via the IRD eTAX portal; (3) provide a beneficial ownership self-declaration through the Form 10 (Ireland? Actually for China, Form DTA 121); (4) submit the TRC and declaration to the PRC payer/withholding agent before the payment date; (5) maintain evidence of economic substance (including office, staff, and decision-making in Hong Kong) to withstand the PRC anti-abuse beneficial ownership test.
stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong does not levy withholding tax on interest. Royalties paid by a Hong Kong user to a non-resident are subject to Hong Kong profits tax at 16.5% on deemed income arising in Hong Kong, unless a double tax treaty reduces or exempts. Under the China–HK DTA, China may impose WHT on interest paid to Hong Kong residents at 7% (domestic rate 10%) and on royalties at 7% (domestic rate 10%). To qualify, the Hong Kong resident must be the beneficial owner.
